reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Definition of Medicare conditions of participation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 2017/2023 (H.B. 402) history notes. Defines 'Medicare conditions of participation' for section 197.005 by referencing 42 CFR 482 for hospitals and 42 CFR 485 for critical access hospitals (42 U.S.C. 1395i-4) and rural emergency hospitals (42 U.S.C. 1395x(kkk)(2)).

headings.title: Deemed compliance with state hospital licensure standards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 2017/2023 history notes. Provides that on and after July 1, 2018, compliance with Medicare conditions of participation is deemed compliance with hospital licensure standards under sections 197.010 to 197.120 and related rules.

headings.title: Authority for separate non-duplicative state regulations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 2017/2023 history notes. Preserves DHSS authority, effective on or after July 1, 2018, to promulgate separate non-duplicative, non-contradictory regulations when specifically authorized by state statute.

headings.title: Expiration of duplicative or conflicting licensure regulations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 2017/2023 history notes. Causes DHSS hospital licensure regulations under chapter 197 that duplicate or conflict with Medicare conditions of participation to lapse and expire on and after July 1, 2018.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and 2017/2023 (H.B. 402) history notes; verified exact source URL, checksums, and all four subsection fingerprints. Checked federal citations (42 CFR 482, 42 CFR 485, 42 U.S.C. 1395i-4, 42 U.S.C. 1395x(kkk)(2)), the July 1, 2018 trigger across subsections 2-4, and the specific-statutory-authorization limit in subsection 3. Retained all four drafted titles.

headings.title: Definition of governmental unit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text, 1953-2023 history notes, and 1995 SSM Health Care annotation. Defines 'governmental unit' as any county, municipality, or other political subdivision or any of its departments, divisions, boards, or agencies.

headings.title: Definition of hospital and chapter 198 exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text, 1953-2023 history notes (including 2023 inclusion of CMS-designated rural emergency hospitals), and 1995 SSM Health Care annotation (holding an outpatient radiation therapy center not open 24 hours is not a hospital). Defines 'hospital' and excludes chapter 198 convalescent, nursing, shelter, and boarding homes.

headings.title: Definition of person
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and section notes. Defines 'person' as any individual, firm, partnership, corporation, company, or association and its legal successors.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three definitions, 1953-2023 history notes (including 2023 inclusion of CMS-designated rural emergency hospitals), and the 1995 SSM Health Care annotation; verified exact checksums and all three subsection fingerprints. Checked the 24-consecutive-hour threshold, chapter 198 exclusion, and successor language. Retained all three drafted titles.

headings.title: Refusal to treat or admit for abortion and immunity
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1973 history note. Provides in archived text that listed medical personnel and public or private hospitals are not required to treat or admit a woman for abortion contrary to policy or moral, ethical, or religious beliefs, and bars causes of action for such refusal.

headings.title: Protection against benefit or employment discrimination for refusal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1973 history note. Bars denying or discriminating against any person or institution in public benefits, assistance, privileges, or public or private employment for refusing to undergo, advise, consent to, assist in, or perform an abortion.

headings.title: Civil liability for discrimination based on abortion refusal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1973 history note. Makes any person who denies or discriminates against another for refusing to perform or participate in an abortion liable to the injured party at law, in equity, or for other redress.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and 1973 history note; verified exact checksums and all three subsection fingerprints. Confirmed neutral descriptive framing of archived conscience-refusal, non-discrimination, and civil-remedy provisions without asserting external enforceability, and verified listed covered personnel and public/private hospital scope. Retained all three drafted titles.

headings.title: Hospital license issuance and annual renewal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1953 history note. Directs DHSS to issue licenses to compliant hospital applicants and provides for annual renewal upon application, fee payment, and department approval unless sooner suspended or revoked.

headings.title: License scope, transfer restrictions, and conspicuous posting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1953 history note. Restricts each license to the named premises and persons or governmental units, prohibits transfer or assignment without DHSS written approval, and requires conspicuous posting on the licensed premises.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and 1953 history note; verified exact checksums and both subsection fingerprints. Revised subsection 2 title from "non-transferability" to "transfer restrictions" because transfer or assignment is allowed with DHSS written approval; retained subsection 1 title covering compliant issuance and annual renewal.

headings.title: Medicare-aligned hospital construction life safety code standards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text, 2016 merged history note, effective-date notes (8-28-16 for S.B. 635/973; 10-14-16 for S.B. 608 after September 14, 2016 veto override), and section 21.250 reference. Directs DHSS to promulgate hospital construction and renovation regulations reflecting exclusively federal Medicare Title XVIII life safety code standards.

headings.title: Facility Guidelines Institute non-mandate and compliance safe harbor
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 2016 veto-override/effective notes. Prohibits requiring hospitals to meet Facility Guidelines Institute design standards while shielding hospitals complying with 2010 or later FGI guidelines from conflicting regulations.

headings.title: Hardship and equivalent-design standard waivers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(2) plus 2016 history notes. Authorizes DHSS waivers of section 197.065 standards for unreasonable hardship without compromising patient health and safety, or where other standards provide equivalent design criteria.

headings.title: Lapse of conflicting hospital licensure regulations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 2016 history notes. Causes DHSS hospital licensure regulations conflicting with subsections 1 and 3 to lapse on and after January 1, 2018.

headings.title: Chapter 536 rulemaking compliance and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and 2016 history notes. Conditions effectiveness of section 197.065 rules on chapter 536 and section 536.028 if applicable, with a nonseverability clause voiding rulemaking authority and rules adopted after August 28, 2016 if legislative rule-review powers are held unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all five subsections including subdivisions 3(1)-(2), 2016 merged history notes, dual effective dates (8-28-16 for S.B. 635/973; 10-14-16 for S.B. 608 under section 21.250 after the September 14, 2016 veto override), and the January 1, 2018 lapse and post-August 28, 2016 nonseverability dates; verified all checksums and fingerprints. Retained all five drafted titles.

headings.title: Hospital licensure rulemaking and section 536.024 compliance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text, 1953-2017 history notes, and July 1, 2018 effective date. Directs DHSS, with state advisory council advice under section 197.005 and chapter 536, to adopt and enforce hospital rules, conditioning effectiveness of sections 197.010 to 197.280 rules on section 536.024 compliance.

headings.title: Regulatory efficiency, CMS alignment, complaints, training, and timelines
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 including lead-in, subdivisions (1)-(5), and paragraphs (3)(a)-(c) plus July 1, 2018 effective note. Directs eliminating duplicative state/CMS rules and inspections and incorporating standards on specific deficiency citations, CMS COP consistency, complaint investigation guidelines and hospital reports, surveyor training participation at hospital cost, and CMS State Operations Manual response timelines.

headings.title: Chapter 536 rulemaking compliance and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and history/effective notes. Conditions effectiveness of section 197.080 rules on chapter 536 and section 536.028 if applicable, declaring nonseverability with post-August 28, 2013 rulemaking void if legislative rule-review powers are held unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections including subdivisions 2(1)-(5) and paragraphs 2(3)(a)-(c), 1953-2017 history notes, and the July 1, 2018 effective date; verified all checksums and fingerprints. Checked section 536.024 scope (sections 197.010 to 197.280), appropriations qualification in 2(2), non-binding CMS timeline guidance in 2(5), and post-August 28, 2013 nonseverability. Retained all three drafted titles.

headings.title: Sole inspection authority, accreditor reports, and scheduling limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1953-2022 history notes. Grants DHSS sole hospital inspection and licensure authority notwithstanding chapters 198 and 338, requires Title XVIII inspections, accepts governmental, Joint Commission, AOA HFAP, and comparable accreditor reports within one year of renewal, and directs avoiding more than one inspection per twelve months absent good cause.

headings.title: Sole department authority over life safety and building codes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1953-2022 history notes. Operates notwithstanding other law to make DHSS the sole state agency determining hospital life safety and building codes, provided new standards apply only to new construction.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and 1953-2022 history notes; verified exact checksums and both subsection fingerprints. Revised subsection 1 title to include the twelve-month inspection scheduling limit (absent good cause) alongside sole DHSS authority and accreditor report acceptance; retained subsection 2 title covering sole DHSS life safety/building code authority (new-construction limit noted).

headings.title: Website posting of substantiated hospital complaint investigations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 including lead-in, subdivisions (1)-(6), and paragraphs (5)(a)-(c) plus 2013 history note. Requires DHSS website posting of substantiated hospital complaints with accepted correction plans, dates, findings, annualized substantiated complaint rates per patient day, peer-group comparisons (psychiatric, 42 CFR 412.23(e) LTACH, 42 CFR 412.29 IRF), and CMS State Operations Manual timelines.

headings.title: Confidentiality limits and section 537.035(4) protections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 2013 history note. Clarifies that section 197.105 neither requires nor permits posting information violating state or federal patient-data or medical-record confidentiality laws or information protected under section 537.035(4), retaining the exact cross-reference without inserting an unstated category label.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections including subdivisions 1(1)-(6) and paragraphs 1(5)(a)-(c) plus 2013 history note; verified all checksums and fingerprints. Revised subsection 2 title and note to remove the unstated inferred label "peer-review" and preserve the exact section 537.035(4) cross-reference; retained subsection 1 title.

headings.title: Two-year bar on assigning former hospital employees as surveyors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 2019 S.B. 514 history note. Prohibits DHSS from assigning an inspector or surveyor to a hospital if employed in the preceding two years by that hospital, its organization, or a competing hospital within fifty miles.

headings.title: Required ten-year employment and family disclosures by surveyors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 including lead-in, subdivisions (1)-(2), continuation paragraph, and 2019 history note. Requires newly hired and existing (as of August 28, 2019) surveyors to disclose ten-year personal and immediate-family hospital employment histories and update disclosures when triggering events first occur.

headings.title: Definition of immediate family member
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 2019 history note. Defines 'immediate family member' for section 197.108 across listed spouse, parent, child, sibling, step-, in-law, grandparent, and grandchild relationships.

headings.title: Public-record status of surveyor disclosures under section 610.010
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 2019 history note. Designates surveyor disclosure information under subsection 2 as a public record under section 610.010.

headings.title: Conflict-of-interest notices, verification, and non-assignment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and 2019 history note. Allows any person to notify DHSS of facts indicating a surveyor's personal or business conflict of interest, requiring verification and non-assignment to the hospital or its organization if DHSS has reason to believe the notice is correct.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all five subsections including subdivisions 2(1)-(2), the subsection 2 continuation paragraph, and 2019 S.B. 514 history note; verified all checksums and fingerprints. Revised subsection 5 title from "surveyor recusal" to "verification, and non-assignment" to match DHSS's verification and non-assignment duty; retained subsections 1-4 titles covering the two-year/fifty-mile bar, ten-year/family disclosures, family definition, and section 610.010 public-record status.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalty for operating an unlicensed hospital
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1953 history note. Makes establishing, conducting, managing, or operating a hospital without a license under the Hospital Licensing Law a misdemeanor.

headings.title: Attorney general representation in actions against unlicensed hospitals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1953 history note. Designates the attorney general to represent DHSS in instituting state actions for injunction or other process against persons or governmental units operating an unlicensed hospital.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and 1953 history note; verified exact checksums and both subsection fingerprints. Revised subsection 2 title to reflect that the attorney general represents DHSS in actions for injunction or other process against persons or governmental units; retained subsection 1 misdemeanor title.

headings.title: Consented forensic examinations, minor consent, and SAFE CARE referrals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text, 2020-2025 history notes, and cross-references to sections 192.2520 and 192.2521. Beginning January 1, 2023 or six months after section 192.2520 telehealth network establishment, requires licensed hospitals to perform consented forensic examinations for sexual-offense victims fourteen or older (applying section 595.220(2) minor consent), requires SAFE CARE referrals under section 334.950 for victims under fourteen (optional for fourteen to seventeen), and preserves optional consented exams for victims under fourteen.

headings.title: Qualified medical providers, training equivalence, and telehealth SANE support
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 including subdivisions (1)-(2) and 2020-2025 history notes. Requires exams by section 595.220 medical providers with training at least equivalent to section 192.2520(4) telehealth training, and requires live telehealth SANE or similarly trained support when the onsite provider lacks that training.

headings.title: Discretionary telehealth waivers for technological or broadband hardship
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and history notes. Permits DHSS to grant sparing, up-to-one-year renewable waivers of subsection 2 telehealth requirements upon written hospital showing of technological or broadband hardship.

headings.title: Waiver when statewide telehealth network ceases operation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and history notes. Requires DHSS to waive section 197.135 requirements when the section 192.2520 telehealth network ceases operation, written notice is issued, and a hospital cannot comply in good faith without network resources, until resumption or independent compliance.

headings.title: Reimbursement of examination costs and evidentiary collection kits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and history notes. Applies section 595.220 to reimbursement of reasonable examination costs and provision of evidentiary collection kits.

headings.title: No-charge telehealth network access prerequisite for hospital compliance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 text and history notes. Excuses individual hospitals from complying with sections 197.135 and 192.2520 unless and until DHSS provides no-charge access to the statewide telehealth network for required mentoring and training.

headings.title: Specialty hospital exemption and definition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 text, 2025 history note, and cross-reference to section 192.2521. Exempts specialty hospitals (defined as licensed hospitals designated other than general acute care hospitals) from sections 197.135 and 192.2520 if they maintain a transfer policy to an appropriate emergency-department hospital.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all seven subsections including subdivisions 2(1)-(2), 2020-2025 history notes, and cross-references to sections 192.2520 and 192.2521; verified all checksums and fingerprints. Revised subsection 1 ("Consented" rather than "Mandatory" to reflect request/consent and contingent network/waiver structure), subsection 3 ("Discretionary" rather than "Annual" for sparing renewable up-to-one-year waivers), and subsection 4 (removed "Mandatory" to avoid flattening the three-part cessation trigger). Retained subsections 2, 5, 6, and 7 titles.

headings.title: Temporary hospital hold of at-risk behavioral health patients
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 2023 H.B. 402 history note. Operates notwithstanding chapter 632 to permit a treating physician at a hospital to temporarily hold a section 190.240 at-risk behavioral health patient for assessment and necessary transfer when reasonably believing the patient poses an imminent serious risk of harm to self or others.

headings.title: Hold duration limit and immediate release upon reassessment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 2023 history note. Limits any temporary hold to the time necessary for evaluation and transfer and mandates immediate release if post-evaluation the treating physician has reasonable cause to believe no imminent serious risk exists.

headings.title: Good-faith civil immunity for hold, treatment, and transport
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 2023 history note. Grants civil immunity to the physician, hospital personnel, EMS personnel, and law enforcement officers acting in good faith and without gross negligence for authorized temporary hold, treatment, or transport actions.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and 2023 H.B. 402 history note; verified exact checksums and all three subsection fingerprints. Checked chapter 632 override, section 190.240 cross-reference, immediate post-evaluation release mandate, and good-faith/without-gross-negligence civil immunity across covered personnel. Retained all three drafted titles.

headings.title: Retaliation protection and reporting interference with infection control
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 2004/2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes. Extends section 197.285 anti-retaliation protections to federally defined infection control officers and hospital, ASC, and abortion facility employees reporting infection control concerns, and requires reporting supervisor interference to the compliance officer.

headings.title: Infection control officer cessation orders and committee review
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 2004/2017 history notes. Authorizes infection control officers to order cessation of non-conforming practices, permits requiring CEO or designee endorsement, requires prompt infection control committee review to sustain or overrule, and directs DHSS documentation rules.

headings.title: Medical staff reporting protections and professional review
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 2004/2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes. Protects medical staff members making good-faith infection control reports from retaliation or discrimination without shielding them from professional review actions for substandard care or policy, rule, or bylaw breaches.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and 2004/2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes; verified exact checksums and all three subsection fingerprints. Revised subsection 3 title and note to use the statute's own term "professional review" instead of "peer review"; retained subsections 1 and 2 titles covering section 197.285 protections, supervisor-interference reporting, cessation orders, CEO endorsement option, and committee review.

headings.title: Definitions for surgical smoke plume evacuation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(4) plus 2023 H.B. 402 history note. Defines 'ambulatory surgical center' (section 197.200), 'hospital' (section 197.020), 'surgical smoke', and 'surgical smoke plume evacuation system' for section 197.185.

headings.title: Required evacuation policies for Joint Commission-accredited facilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 2023 history note. Requires Joint Commission-accredited hospitals and ambulatory surgical centers performing smoke-plume procedures to adopt and implement Joint Commission policies using evacuation systems for energy-based device procedures on or before January 1, 2026.

headings.title: Post-2025 applicability to energy-based surgical procedures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 2023 history note. Subjects energy-based device procedures generating surgical smoke plume performed after December 31, 2025 in Joint Commission-accredited hospitals or ASCs to subsection 2 policies.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections including subdivisions 1(1)-(4) and 2023 H.B. 402 history note; verified exact checksums and fingerprints. Checked Joint Commission accreditation limitation, January 1, 2026 policy deadline, and post-December 31, 2025 procedure applicability. Retained all three drafted titles.

headings.title: State license requirement for surgical centers and abortion facilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1975-2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes. Prohibits any person or governmental unit from establishing, conducting, or maintaining an ambulatory surgical center or abortion facility without a DHSS license under sections 197.200 to 197.240; describes archived text without asserting current enforceability.

headings.title: Preserved local licensing authority subject to state standards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1975-2017 history notes. Preserves governmental unit licensing authority over ambulatory surgical centers and abortion facilities provided local ordinances require compliance with all DHSS rules and standards under sections 197.200 to 197.240.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and 1975-2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes; verified exact checksums and both subsection fingerprints. Confirmed neutral framing of archived ASC and abortion facility state licensing and preserved local-ordinance authority subject to state compliance. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: License application forms and compliance evidence
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1975/1982 history note. Directs applying to DHSS on department-provided forms and authorizes requiring affirmative evidence of ability to comply with sections 197.200 to 197.240 standards.

headings.title: Annual license fee, governmental exemption, and treasury deposit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1975/1982 history note. Requires a two-hundred-dollar annual license fee with each application except governmental unit applications, deposited to the state general revenue fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and 1975/1982 history note; verified exact checksums and both subsection fingerprints. Revised subsection 2 title to encompass the annual license fee, governmental unit exemption, and general revenue treasury deposit concisely; retained subsection 1 title.

headings.title: Licensure prerequisites for staffing, hospital continuity, and records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(4) plus 1975-2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes. Requires affirmative evidence of Missouri-licensed surgical and abortion staff, ASC hospital surgical privileges or emergency transfer working agreements, continuous physician or RN services while patients are present, and adequate patient medical records.

headings.title: Annual license issuance, renewal, and scope
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1975-2017 history notes. Directs DHSS to issue or renew compliant one-year licenses limited to the named persons and premises unless sooner suspended or revoked.

headings.title: Restriction on license transfer and conspicuous posting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1975-2017 history notes. Limits each license to named premises and persons or governmental units, bars transfer or assignment without DHSS written consent, and requires conspicuous posting.

headings.title: New license required upon transfer of operational responsibilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 1975-2017 history notes. Requires applying for a new license effective on the transfer date whenever an ASC or abortion facility licensee legally transfers operational responsibilities to another section 197.200 person.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections including subdivisions 1(1)-(4) and 1975-2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes; verified all checksums and fingerprints. Checked distinction between subsection 2 (issuance/renewal, one-year term, named persons/premises) and subsection 3 (written consent transfer restriction and posting) plus subsection 4 operational-responsibility transfers. Retained all four drafted titles.

headings.title: Department rulemaking authority and listed patient-safety standards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(5) plus 1975-2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes. Authorizes DHSS rules and standards under sections 197.200 to 197.240 covering facility construction, staffing, equipment, ASC programs/services, and peer-review and complaint procedures.

headings.title: Separate regulatory standards for surgical centers and abortion facilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 2017 effective-date note. Authorizes DHSS to adopt separate rules, regulations, or standards for ambulatory surgical centers and for abortion facilities.

headings.title: Written emergency and hospital-transfer protocols for abortion facilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 2017 effective-date note. Requires abortion facilities to maintain a written protocol for managing medical emergencies and transferring patients needing further emergency care to a hospital within a reasonable distance.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections including subdivisions 1(1)-(5) and 1975-2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes; verified all checksums and fingerprints. Checked permissive rulemaking language in subsections 1-2, ASC-specific wording in 1(4)-(5), and written emergency/transfer protocol requirement for abortion facilities in subsection 3. Retained all three drafted titles.

headings.title: Department inspection authority and local delegation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1975/2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes. Directs DHSS inspections and investigations and allows delegating ASC or abortion facility inspection authority to a qualified official of a political subdivision with at least 450,000 population.

headings.title: Annual unannounced on-site inspections of abortion facilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(3) plus 2017 effective-date note. Mandates at least annual unannounced on-site abortion facility inspections covering statutory/regulatory and emergency readiness requirements, chapter 188 compliance, and section 197.215 continuous physician or RN coverage.

headings.title: Public availability of reports and permitted redactions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 2017 effective-date note. Makes inspection, investigation, and quality assurance reports publicly available while allowing redaction of portions not subject to disclosure under law.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections including subdivisions 2(1)-(3) and 1975/2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes; verified all checksums and fingerprints. Noted archived source nuance in subsection 1 allowing delegation for ASCs or abortion facilities where the >=450,000 political subdivision is deemed qualified to inspect ASCs, and checked annual unannounced abortion facility inspections and permitted redactions. Retained all three drafted titles.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor and separate daily offenses for unlicensed operation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1975-2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes. Makes operating an unlicensed ASC or abortion facility a class A misdemeanor carrying up to a five-hundred-dollar fine, with each continuing day constituting a separate offense.

headings.title: Attorney general actions to restrain unlicensed facilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1975-2017 history notes. Directs the attorney general to represent DHSS and bring injunctive or other relief actions restraining unlicensed ASC or abortion facility operations.

headings.title: Daily fine for advertising falsely implying state involvement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1975-2017 history notes. Imposes a one-hundred-dollar daily fine on ASC or abortion facility operators using listed Missouri or DHSS names, initials, or emblems in advertising calculated to falsely imply state involvement.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and 1975-2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes; verified exact checksums and all three subsection fingerprints. Revised subsection 1 title to distinguish separate daily criminal offenses (up to $500 upon conviction) from subsection 3's $100/day advertising fine, and revised subsection 2 title to cover injunctive or other relief actions. Retained subsection 3 title.

headings.title: Certificate required to provide or advertise hospice care
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1992 history note. Prohibits providing hospice care or holding oneself out as a hospice without a certificate under sections 197.250 to 197.280.

headings.title: Professionally accepted standards for hospice skilled care
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1992 history note. Requires all skilled care provided by a hospice to meet professionally accepted standards.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and 1992 history note; verified exact checksums and both subsection fingerprints. Confirmed certificate requirement for providing hospice care or holding out as a hospice under sections 197.250 to 197.280 and professionally accepted skilled-care standard. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: Certificate application, sliding-scale fee, and no-charge exemption
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1992/1996 history note. Requires written DHSS hospice certification applications with a sliding-scale fee of $250 to $750 set with advisory council input, and exempts entities exacting no charge from sections 197.250 to 197.280.

headings.title: Temporary operating permits and named-applicant scope
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1992/1996 history note. Authorizes temporary operating permits pending application approval and limits permits and certificates solely to the listed person or entity.

headings.title: Pre-certification department survey and certificate issuance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1992/1996 history note. Requires DHSS to survey service quality upon receiving the application and any required fee and issue a certificate to compliant applicants passing survey.

headings.title: Conspicuous posting of permit or certificate in main office
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 1992/1996 history note. Requires hospices to post their temporary operating permit or certificate conspicuously in the main office.

headings.title: Certificate renewal under section 197.256
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and 1992/1996 history note. Subjects section 197.254 certificates to renewal as provided in section 197.256.

headings.title: Board of pharmacy licensure for hospice-operated pharmacies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 text and 1992/1996 history note. Requires any pharmacy operated by a licensed hospice to be licensed and inspected by the board of pharmacy under chapter 338.

headings.title: Proximity and shared administration for hospice branch offices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 text and 1992/1996 history note. Requires branch offices to be sufficiently close to share administration, supervision, and services so separate certification is unnecessary except as otherwise provided in sections 197.250 to 197.280.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all seven subsections and 1992/1996 history note; verified exact checksums and all seven subsection fingerprints. Checked $250-$750 sliding-scale fee, no-charge exemption, discretionary temporary permit, pre-certification survey, main-office posting, section 197.256 renewal cross-reference, chapter 338 pharmacy licensure (retaining source "licensed hospice" term), and branch-office proximity. Retained all seven drafted titles.

headings.title: Annual renewal and thirty-day ownership or management change filing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1992/2022 history note. Requires hospice certificate renewal applications at least every twelve months and at least thirty days before any ownership or management change, accompanied by the section 197.254(1) fee.

headings.title: Renewal survey, Title XVIII inspection, and approval
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1992/2022 history note. Authorizes renewal quality surveys, mandates inspections under Title XVIII of the Social Security Act, and directs renewal for compliant hospices passing survey.

headings.title: Void status of unrenewed hospice certificates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1992/2022 history note. Declares the certificate of any hospice not renewed as required by section 197.256 to be void.

headings.title: Required statistical reports from certificated hospices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 1992/2022 history note. Requires certificated hospices to submit statistical reports in the content, format, and frequency prescribed by DHSS.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and 1992/2022 history note; verified exact checksums and all four subsection fingerprints. Checked 12-month renewal and 30-day ownership/management change deadlines, discretionary renewal survey alongside mandatory Title XVIII inspection (retaining source "licensed facility" wording), void unrenewed status, and statistical reports. Retained all four drafted titles.

headings.title: Hospice surveys, Title XVIII standard, and premises access
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1992/2022 history note. Authorizes additional DHSS surveys during normal business hours, requires surveying every hospice in accordance with Title XVIII of the Social Security Act, and requires premises entry access.

headings.title: Consensual visits to hospice clients' homes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1992/2022 history note. Authorizes DHSS to visit a hospice client's home as part of a survey with the client's consent.

headings.title: Acceptance of comparable agency or accreditor surveys
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(2) plus 1992/2022 history note. Allows DHSS to accept state, federal, or professional accrediting agency surveys in lieu of required surveys if comparable in scope and method and conducted under Title XVIII.

headings.title: Survey exemption for reciprocal bordering-state hospices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 1992/2022 history note. Relieves DHSS from surveying hospices serving Missouri residents from a bordering-state office when a reciprocal certification agreement exists and the Missouri service area is contiguous.

headings.title: Missouri branch office requirement for non-reciprocal out-of-state hospices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and 1992/2022 history note. Requires hospices with parent offices in non-reciprocal states to maintain a certificated Missouri branch office holding all survey records.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all five subsections including subdivisions 3(1)-(2) and 1992/2022 history note; verified all checksums and fingerprints. Revised subsection 1 title to cover additional business-hours surveys, Title XVIII survey standard, and premises access; retained subsections 2-5 titles covering consensual home visits, comparable accreditor/agency surveys, reciprocal bordering-state exemption, and certificated Missouri branch office requirement.

headings.title: Survey deficiency reports, service, and ten-day correction plans
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1992 history note. Directs DHSS to serve a written compliance report and statute/rule deficiency list within fifteen working days after survey completion and requires the hospice to submit compliance timing and a correction plan within ten days excluding weekends and state holidays.

headings.title: Public disclosure of final survey reports and confidentiality
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1992 history note. Permits public disclosure of final inspection/survey reports showing standards, findings, and correction plans, while keeping all other collected, derived, or accreditor-submitted information confidential except to the surveyed entity.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and 1992 history note; verified exact checksums and both subsection fingerprints. Checked 15-working-day report service, 10-day correction plan (excluding weekends and state holidays), discretionary public disclosure of final reports, and broad confidentiality of other collected/derived/accreditor information. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: Grounds for certificate denial, suspension, revocation, or sanctions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(2) plus 1992 history note. Authorizes DHSS to deny certification or renewal, suspend or revoke a certificate, or invoke intermediate sanctions for noncompliance with sections 197.250 to 197.280/rules or obtaining a certificate by misrepresentation or concealment.

headings.title: Administrative hearing commission review under chapter 621
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1992 history note. Allows a hospice to seek chapter 621 administrative hearing commission review of any denial, suspension, or revocation of certification or renewal.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections including subdivisions 1(1)-(2) and 1992 history note; verified exact checksums and both subsection fingerprints. Checked discretionary denial, suspension, revocation, and intermediate sanctions in subsection 1 versus chapter 621 AHC review of denial, suspension, or revocation in subsection 2. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: Department-approved hospice client bill of rights
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1992 history note. Requires DHSS approval of an equally applicable client bill of rights covering care alternatives, provider choice, charges/payment resources, care-plan participation, and dignity/respect, plus providing copies and ensuring delivery of rights.

headings.title: Ongoing discharge planning and reasonable discharge notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1992 history note. Makes discharge planning an ongoing hospice responsibility including reasonable notice of discharge to the client, responsible party, or both.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and 1992 history note; verified exact checksums and both subsection fingerprints. Checked DHSS approval, minimum rights, client copy, and delivery assurance for the bill of rights, plus ongoing discharge planning and reasonable discharge notice. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: Establishment and advisory role of state hospice advisory council
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1992/2002 history note. Establishes the State Hospice Advisory Council to guide, advise, and make recommendations to DHSS.

headings.title: Council size, citizenship, residency, and hospice sector representation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(3) plus history note. Requires five U.S.-citizen, one-year-Missouri-resident members experienced with hospices, including at least one each from home-health-based, hospital-based, and rural-based hospices.

headings.title: Director appointments, five-year terms, vacancies, and officers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and history note. Provides for DHSS director appointment for five-year terms, pre-expiration successor appointments, unexpired-term vacancy filling, and annual council designation of chairperson and secretary.

headings.title: Two-term limit and one-year waiting period for reappointment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and history note. Bars reappointing any council member who has served two full terms until at least one year after expiration of the most recent full term.

headings.title: Uncompensated service and appropriated expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and history note. Provides no compensation for council service while allowing reimbursement of actual and necessary expenses subject to appropriations.

headings.title: Policy consultation and pre-promulgation review of hospice rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(2) plus history note. Directs the council to consult with DHSS on policy and rule development under sections 197.250 to 197.280 and review and recommend on rules and standards prior to promulgation.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all six subsections including subdivisions 2(1)-(3) and 6(1)-(2) plus 1992/2002 history note; verified all checksums and fingerprints. Checked five-member hospice sector composition, director appointments, five-year terms, two-term/one-year waiting period, subject-to-appropriations expenses, and pre-promulgation rule review. Retained all six drafted titles.

headings.title: Written employee-disclosure policies and compliance officers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(3) plus 2000-2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes. Requires hospitals, ASCs, and abortion facilities to adopt and submit written employee-disclosure protection policies with thirty-day investigation limits, disposition notices, non-interference/anti-retaliation bars, and designated primary and alternate compliance officers.

headings.title: Protected good-faith disclosures, department access, and complainant notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 including lead-in, subdivisions (1)-(3), continuation paragraph, and effective-date note. Covers good-faith employee disclosures of mismanagement/fraud, patient/facility safety law violations, or duty-performance barriers, ensures continuous DHSS access and annual review, and mandates notifying complainants of DHSS access and reporting rights.

headings.title: Internal reporting prerequisite before non-department external disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and history notes. Requires employees making disclosures under section 197.285 to report first to designated facility officials before disclosing to individuals or agencies other than DHSS.

headings.title: Seven-day facility duty to report credible evidence of misconduct
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and history notes. Requires facilities discovering credible evidence of potential criminal, civil, or administrative law violations after reasonable inquiry to report to appropriate governmental authorities within seven days.

headings.title: Section 197.477 restrictions and preserved employee subpoena rights
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and history notes. Subjects DHSS reports to section 197.477 while clarifying that section 197.477 restrictions do not limit an employee's ability to subpoena reported information from the original source.

headings.title: Anonymous reporting and employee, patient, and record safeguards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 text and history notes. Requires written policies to allow anonymous employee reports and include safeguards for employee and patient confidentiality and data/medical-record integrity.

headings.title: Forty-eight-hour acknowledgment of employee report receipt
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 text and history notes. Requires facilities within forty-eight hours of receiving an employee report to notify the employee that it was received and is being reviewed.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all seven subsections including subdivisions 1(1)-(3), 2(1)-(3), the subsection 2 continuation paragraph, and 2000-2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes; verified all checksums and fingerprints. Revised subsection 1 title to replace non-statutory "whistleblower" with neutral "employee-disclosure" phrasing and revised subsection 5 title and note to match "restrictions of section 197.477" faithfully. Retained subsections 2, 3, 4, 6, and 7 titles.

headings.title: Nurse staffing methodology and continuous registered nurse coverage
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 2000/2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes. Requires hospitals, ASCs, and abortion facilities to implement adequate nurse staffing methodologies maintaining sufficient licensed RNs on duty at all times to deliver RN care and oversee nursing personnel.

headings.title: Unit-level licensed and ancillary nursing staffing standards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 2000/2017 history notes. Requires sufficient licensed and ancillary nursing personnel on duty on each nursing unit to meet patient needs under accepted quality-care standards.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and 2000/2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes; verified exact checksums and both subsection fingerprints. Checked covered facilities (hospitals, ASCs, abortion facilities), continuous licensed RN coverage, and unit-level licensed and ancillary staffing. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: Graduated licensure enforcement steps for continuing deficiencies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 including lead-in, subdivisions (1)-(5), and paragraphs (2)(a)-(b) plus 2000-2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes. Sets progressive DHSS enforcement steps (approved correction plan, follow-up or department-developed plan, restricting new admissions/entrants, suspending affected services, and license denial/suspension/revocation under section 197.070 or 197.220).

headings.title: Service access restrictions for immediate and serious patient threats
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 2000-2017 history notes. Operates notwithstanding subsection 1 to let DHSS restrict access to affected services for immediate and serious patient health/safety threats until an approved correction plan is implemented, under regulatory guidelines approved by the licensing bureau or authorized official.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections including subdivisions 1(1)-(5), paragraphs 1(2)(a)-(b), and 2000-2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes; verified all checksums and fingerprints. Revised subsection 2 title to "Service access restrictions for immediate and serious patient threats" to avoid redundant wording and clarify service-specific discretionary restriction; retained subsection 1 graduated enforcement title.

headings.title: Appeals, judicial review, expedited hearings, and stay requests
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 2000/2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes. Authorizes AHC appeals under section 197.071 or 197.221 and section 621.145 judicial review for specified section 197.293(1) enforcement decisions, requiring expedited hearings for admission restrictions, service suspensions, or revocations and allowing section 621.035 stay applications.

headings.title: Optional mutually agreed departmental hearing officer appeal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 2000/2017 history notes. Permits appealing official actions under sections 197.010 to 197.120 or 197.200 to 197.240 to a departmental hearing officer prior to AHC appeal if both DHSS and the facility agree, under DHSS rules ensuring qualifications and impartiality.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and 2000/2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes; verified exact checksums and both subsection fingerprints. Revised subsection 1 title to include section 621.145 judicial review and clarify stay applications ("stay requests") alongside AHC appeals and expedited hearings; retained subsection 2 mutually agreed departmental hearing officer title.

headings.title: Department rulemaking authority for sections 197.287 to 197.297
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 2000 history note. Authorizes DHSS to adopt rules necessary to implement sections 197.287 to 197.297.

headings.title: Chapter 536 rulemaking compliance and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 2000 history note. Conditions effectiveness of sections 197.287 to 197.297 rules on chapter 536 and section 536.028 if applicable, declaring nonseverability with post-August 28, 2000 rulemaking void if legislative rule-review powers are held unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and 2000 history note; verified exact checksums and both subsection fingerprints. Checked sections 197.287 to 197.297 rulemaking scope, chapter 536 and section 536.028 compliance, and post-August 28, 2000 nonseverability clause. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: Establishment and staffing of health facilities review committee
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text, 1979/1999 history note, and July 1, 1999 effective date. Establishes the Missouri Health Facilities Review Committee with agency clerical/administrative support and authority to employ additional staff.

headings.title: Committee membership and political party balance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(3) plus 1979/1999 history note. Composes the nine-member committee of two bipartisan senators, two bipartisan house members, and five governor-appointed, senate-confirmed members (no more than three from one party).

headings.title: Majority quorum required to conduct committee business
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and history note. Prohibits performing any committee business without a majority of the full body.

headings.title: Initial staggered expirations and two-year member terms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and history note. Sets initial post-September 28, 1979 appointments expiring January 1, 1981 and January 1, 1982, with all subsequent members serving two-year terms.

headings.title: Chairman election and calling of committee meetings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and history note. Directs electing a chairman at the governor-called first meeting and meeting thereafter upon call of the chairman or governor.

headings.title: Certificate of need application review and procedural rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 text and history note. Empowers the committee to review and approve or disapprove all sections 197.300 to 197.366 certificate of need applications and issue reasonable application rules.

headings.title: Uncompensated committee service and necessary expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 text and history note. Provides that committee members serve without compensation but are reimbursed for necessary official expenses.

headings.title: Proceedings and records subject to chapter 610
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 8 text, history note, and footnote noting section 610.025 was repealed by S.B. 2, 1987 (retained as archived). Subjects committee proceedings and records to chapter 610 notwithstanding archived reference to section 610.025(4).

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all eight subsections including subdivisions 2(1)-(3), 1979/1999 (effective 7-1-99) history notes, and the footnote noting repeal of section 610.025 by S.B. 2, 1987; verified all checksums and fingerprints. Revised subsection 8 title to "Proceedings and records subject to chapter 610" to stay strictly faithful to source wording while retaining the repealed 610.025(4) reference in notes. Retained subsections 1-7 titles.

headings.title: Certificate of need required before offering new health services
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1979-2026 (H.B. 2372) history notes. Requires obtaining a committee certificate of need before offering any proposed new institutional health service in Missouri.

headings.title: Finding of need and expenditure minimum prerequisite
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1979-2026 history notes. Limits certificates of need and service development to services found needed by the committee and bars expenditures above the applicable expenditure minimum without a certificate.

headings.title: Bar on licensing or certifying facilities lacking certificate of need
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and history notes. Bars state licensing or certifying agencies after October 1, 1980 from licensing or certifying any health care facility or distinct part developed without a certificate of need.

headings.title: Attorney general enforcement against unauthorized service development
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and history notes. Directs the committee to notify the attorney general, who shall seek injunctive or other legal action against anyone proposing to develop a new institutional health care service without a required certificate.

headings.title: Bar on state agency funding without required certificates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and history notes. Prohibits state government agencies after October 1, 1980 from appropriating, granting, or paying funds to any person or facility lacking every required certificate of need.

headings.title: Named premises and persons scope and transfer restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 text and history notes. Restricts certificates of need to named premises and persons and bars transfer without committee consent.

headings.title: Committee consent required for project cost overruns above ten percent
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 text and history notes. Prohibits incurring project cost increases exceeding the initial estimate by more than ten percent due to application changes or change orders without committee consent.

headings.title: Periodic project progress reports and forfeiture for nonfiling
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 8 text and history notes. Requires periodic reports to the committee until project completion and permits ordering forfeiture for failure to file.

headings.title: Six-month capital expenditure deadline, forfeiture, and extension
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 9 text and history notes. Subjects certificates to forfeiture if no capital expenditure is incurred within six months after the order, allowing one extension of up to six additional months based on substantial expenditure.

headings.title: Application fees, filing start time, and committee appropriations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 10 text and history notes. Requires an application fee of the greater of $1,000 or 0.1% of total project cost (starting filing time on receipt of both application and fee), treasury deposit, and general assembly committee appropriations.

headings.title: Fifteen-mile radius limit on considering competing facilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 11 text and history notes. Bars considering facilities or equipment of other health care facilities located more than fifteen miles from the applying facility.

headings.title: Nursing facility return from intermediate to skilled level without certificate
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 12 text and history notes. Permits a nursing facility that shifted from skilled to intermediate nursing care to return to the higher level without a certificate of need if meeting licensure requirements.

headings.title: Prohibition on denial for refusing abortion services or information
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 13 text and history notes. Prohibits denying a certificate of need because an applicant refuses to provide abortion services or information.

headings.title: Exemption for transferring ownership of entire operational facility
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 14 text and history notes. Exempts transferring ownership of an existing and operational health facility in its entirety from certificate of need requirements.

headings.title: Authority to grant partial or reduced certificate of need
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 15 text and history notes. Permits granting a certificate of need for an expansion, added service, new institutional service, or new hospital providing less than requested in the application.

headings.title: State-operated facility exemption and state hospital carve-out
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 16 text and 2026 H.B. 2372 amendment note. Exempts state-operated facilities funded by legislative appropriation without fee, while carving out state-operated hospitals licensed under chapter 197 except DMH state-operated psychiatric hospitals.

headings.title: Intermediate care facilities exclusively for intellectually disabled
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 17 text and history notes. Operates notwithstanding other provisions of section 197.315 to permit issuing a certificate of need after July 1, 1983 for an intermediate care facility operated exclusively for the intellectually disabled.

headings.title: Exemptions for clinical-trial research and state academic equipment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 18 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(2) plus history notes. Exempts purchasing and operating IRB-approved clinical-trial research equipment not increasing bed complement (requiring a certificate for post-trial use) and research/teaching equipment of state-operated academic health centers.

headings.title: Rescission for material facts withheld or misrepresented
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 19 text and history notes. Directs the committee, if within thirty days of an applicant receiving a certificate of need (including on appeal) it obtains evidence that a material fact was withheld or misrepresented at the original hearing, to vote at its next regularly scheduled meeting to rescind the certificate and require a corrected new application.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all nineteen subsections including subdivisions 18(1)-(2) and 1979-2026 (H.B. 2372) history notes; verified exact checksums and all nineteen subsection fingerprints. Revised subsection 4 (to include "other appropriate legal action"), subsection 6 ("transfer restrictions" reflecting committee-consent exception), subsection 17 (specifying "Intermediate care facilities"), and subsection 19 (avoiding misstating the 30-day evidence window as the rescission vote deadline). Checked 2026 state-hospital carve-out with DMH psychiatric exception in subsection 16 and retained the other fifteen drafted titles.

headings.title: Exemption from 197.315(10), 197.317, and 197.318 for AIDS facilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text, 1995/1999 history note, and July 1, 1999 effective date. Despite the Revisor catchline, the statutory text of subsection 1 exempts qualifying chapter 198 AIDS-only facilities specifically from section 197.315(10) and archived references to sections 197.317 (repealed) and 197.318.

headings.title: Restriction limiting exempt facilities exclusively to AIDS patients
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and July 1, 1999 effective note. Requires facilities granted a certificate of need and found exempt under subsection 1 to admit only AIDS patients and no others.

headings.title: Daily per-resident fine for admitting non-AIDS residents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and July 1, 1999 effective note. Imposes a one-hundred-dollar per-resident, per-day fine on any facility violating subsection 2.

headings.title: Attorney general enforcement upon department request
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and July 1, 1999 effective note. Directs the attorney general, upon DHSS request, to bring a circuit court action for violations of section 197.316.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections, 1995/1999 history note, and July 1, 1999 effective date; verified exact checksums and all four subsection fingerprints. Revised subsection 1 title and note to preserve the exact statutory scope—exempting qualifying chapter 198 AIDS-only facilities from section 197.315(10) and archived references to sections 197.317 (repealed) and 197.318—rather than echoing the broader Revisor catchline. Retained subsections 2-4 titles.

headings.title: Definition of licensed and available beds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1986-2014 history notes. Defines 'licensed and available' for section 197.318 as beds actually in place for which a license has been issued.

headings.title: Review of long-term care hospital bed letters and applications
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and history notes. Directs the committee to review letters of intent and applications for 42 CFR 412.23(e) long-term care hospital beds under its long-term care bed criteria and standards.

headings.title: Exclusion for state litigation pending by April 1, 1996
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and history notes. Excludes state-court litigation pending on or before April 1, 1996 naming the committee as defendant regarding 42 CFR 412.23(e) long-term care hospital beds from sections 197.300 to 197.366.

headings.title: Chapter 198 bed expansion, purchase, sale, and relocation rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 including lead-in, subdivisions (1)-(5), and nested paragraphs (1)(a)-(e) plus history notes. Establishes chapter 198 bed expansion via letter of intent, eighteen-month purchase effort, occupancy/deficiency certification, purchase or formula expansion caps, five-year seller non-use and expansion bars, two-year seller inventory attribution, and six-mile residential care relocation.

headings.title: Private-room replacement of half of licensed beds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(3) plus history notes (retaining archived 'to the health and senior services' wording in (1)). Allows long-term care facilities operating at fifty percent capacity in private rooms for four consecutive quarters to replace half their licensed beds within thirty miles under single-occupancy and written non-use stipulations.

headings.title: Full chapter 198 facility replacement within fifteen miles
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 text and history notes. Permits replacing an entire chapter 198 facility within fifteen miles under the same ownership provided the replaced facility remains unlicensed and unused for any long-term care services.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all six subsections including subdivisions 4(1)-(5), nested paragraphs 4(1)(a)-(e), subdivisions 5(1)-(3), and 1986-2014 history notes; verified all checksums and fingerprints. Revised subsection 3 title ("by April 1, 1996" to include April 1 itself) and subsection 5 title (replacing ambiguous "Half-bed" and covering same-site or within-30-mile replacement). Retained archived source nuances without alteration: 40-bed boundary gap in 4(1)(e), DSS reference in 4(3), and omitted "department of" in 5(1). Retained subsections 1, 2, 4, and 6 titles.

headings.title: Lobbyist and project-interest registration and section 105.478 penalties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text, 1992/2014 history note, and January 1, 2017 effective date. Requires paid supporters or opponents of projects before the committee to register as chapter 105 lobbyists and register per-project support/opposition and represented parties with committee staff, subject to section 105.478 penalties.

headings.title: Pending-application contribution ban for legislative committee members
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and January 1, 2017 effective note. Prohibits general assembly members serving on the health facilities review committee from soliciting or accepting campaign contributions from applicants, opponents, or their speakers while an application is pending.

headings.title: Gift and contribution ban for regulated entities and criminal penalties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and January 1, 2017 effective note. Bars chapter 197 or 198 regulated persons and their officers, attorneys, agents, and employees from offering offices, gifts, entertainment, gratuities, or campaign contributions to committee members or staff while an application is pending, and sets class B misdemeanor first-offense and class E felony repeat-offense penalties for knowingly violating "the provisions of this section" (source wording retained).

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections, 1992/2014 history note, and January 1, 2017 effective date; verified exact checksums and all three subsection fingerprints. Revised subsection 2 title to qualify the contribution ban to pending applications and revised subsection 3 title and note to distinguish criminal penalties (knowingly violating "this section" in archived text) from subsection 1's section 105.478 penalties. Retained subsection 1 title.

headings.title: Exclusive Medicaid-patient use of Medicaid-need certificate beds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1988 history note. Restricts additional beds approved under sections 197.300 to 197.365 based on a stated need for Medicaid beds exclusively to Medicaid patients.

headings.title: Daily civil penalties for non-Medicaid patient placements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1988 history note. Imposes a one-hundred-dollar per-day civil penalty payable to the state for subsection 1 violations, with each non-Medicaid patient placed in a Medicaid bed constituting a separate violation.

headings.title: Circuit court enforcement and venue for penalty recovery
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1988 history note. Directs the attorney general upon department request—or permits the department directly—to sue in Cole County circuit court or another county with venue to recover civil penalties.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and 1988 history note; verified exact checksums and all three subsection fingerprints. Retained archived cross-reference to "sections 197.300 to 197.365" in subsection 1 without alteration, and verified per-patient daily civil penalties and AG/department enforcement with Cole County or alternate venue. Retained all three drafted titles.

headings.title: Committee review duties, timelines, hearings, and filing definition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 including lead-in, subdivisions (1)-(8), continuation paragraph defining 'filed'/'filing', 1979-1999 history notes (effective 7-1-99), and 1987 Platte County Medical Center annotation. Details completeness notice (15 days), affected-person notice, requested public hearings (30 days), written decision (100 days plus up to 30-day extension), service, training/osteopathic considerations, and nonsubstantive project rules.

headings.title: Approval by operation of law for missed decision deadline
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text, effective-date note, and 1987 Platte County Medical Center annotation. Makes failure to issue a timely written decision final administrative approval, appealable under section 197.335 solely on approval by operation of law.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections including subdivisions 1(1)-(8), the subsection 1 continuation paragraph defining "filed"/"filing", 1979-1999 (effective 7-1-99) history notes, and the 1987 Platte County Medical Center annotation; verified all checksums and fingerprints. Checked timelines, archived "health system agency" term in 1(5), and limited section 197.335 appeal scope in subsection 2. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: Written home health agency license application
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1983 history note. Requires persons seeking a Missouri home health agency license to file a written application with DHSS on a director-prescribed form.

headings.title: Six-hundred-dollar license application fee
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1983 history note. Requires a six-hundred-dollar license fee to accompany the home health agency license application.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and 1983 history note; verified exact checksums and both subsection fingerprints. Revised subsection 2 title to remove unstated word "initial" so it strictly matches the archived text; retained subsection 1 title.

headings.title: Application review and home health license issuance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1983-2022 history notes. Directs DHSS to review applications and issue licenses to compliant and approved home health agency applicants under sections 197.400 to 197.475.

headings.title: Annual renewal fee, Title XVIII inspection, and change statement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(3) plus 1983-2022 history notes. Conditions annual renewal upon DHSS approval, a six-hundred-dollar fee, compliance evidenced by a Title XVIII inspection, and a statement of changes to section 197.410 information.

headings.title: Named-agency license scope and main-office posting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1983-2022 history notes. Limits each license to the listed home health agency and requires conspicuous posting in its main offices.

headings.title: Acceptance of comparable agency or accreditor survey reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(2) plus 1997/2022 history notes. Permits DHSS to accept written survey reports of state, federal, or professional accrediting agencies if comparable in scope and method and conducted under Title XVIII.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections including subdivisions 2(1)-(3) and 4(1)-(2) plus 1983-2022 history notes; verified all checksums and fingerprints. Revised subsection 1 title to remove unstated word "initial" while keeping clear distinction from subsection 2 annual renewal; retained subsections 2, 3, and 4 titles covering renewal conditions, named-agency scope/posting, and comparable survey report acceptance.

headings.title: Grounds for home health license refusal, suspension, or revocation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1983 history note. Directs DHSS to refuse, suspend, or revoke a home health agency license for noncompliance with sections 197.400 to 197.475 or department rules/standards, or obtaining a license by fraud, misrepresentation, or material concealment.

headings.title: Administrative hearing commission review of adverse licensing actions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1983 history note. Allows a home health agency whose license is refused, revoked, or suspended to seek review by the administrative hearing commission.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and 1983 history note; verified exact checksums and both subsection fingerprints. Revised subsection 1 title to remove awkward "Mandatory grounds" phrasing while preserving the statutory "shall" framing in the review note; retained subsection 2 AHC review title.

headings.title: Department rulemaking authority and federal Title XVIII floor
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1983-2022 history notes. Authorizes reasonable rules and standards for sections 197.400 to 197.477 at least equal to federal Title XVIII home health agency standards, initially promulgated within one year of September 28, 1983.

headings.title: Scope of covered services, ordering practitioners, and section 536.024
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1983-2022 history notes. Applies DHSS rules to all covered home health services regardless of payment source, condition, or residence when ordered by a physician, podiatrist, nurse practitioner, clinical nurse specialist, or physician assistant, conditioning rule effectiveness on section 536.024.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and 1983-2022 history notes; verified exact checksums and both subsection fingerprints. Revised subsection 2 title to replace overbroad "Universal service applicability" with accurate scope covering covered home health services, listed ordering practitioners (expanded in 2022), and section 536.024 compliance; retained subsection 1 title.

headings.title: Creation and advisory role of home health services advisory council
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1983/2002 history note. Creates the Home Health Services Advisory Council to guide, advise, and make recommendations to DHSS on rules, standards, and administration of sections 197.400 to 197.475.

headings.title: Council residency, term limits, chair, and stakeholder composition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(5) plus 1983/2002 history note. Requires state-resident members serving three-year terms (maximum two successive full terms), including a DHSS representative chair, three unaffiliated public members, and five members representing listed public, institutional, voluntary nonprofit, private nonprofit, and for-profit home health agencies.

headings.title: Director appointments, initial staggered terms, and vacancies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1983/2002 history note. Provides for DHSS director appointment for three-year terms (staggered 1-3 years initially), pre-expiration successor appointments, and unexpired-term vacancy filling.

headings.title: Quarterly meeting minimum and special meeting calls
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 1983/2002 history note. Requires at least quarterly council meetings and permits additional meetings called by the chairman or a majority of other members.

headings.title: Uncompensated service and appropriated expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and 1983/2002 history note. Provides no compensation for council service while allowing reimbursement of actual and necessary expenses subject to appropriations.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all five subsections including subdivisions 2(1)-(5) and 1983/2002 history note; verified all checksums and fingerprints. Checked nine-member composition (DHSS chair, three at-large citizens, five agency-type representatives), three-year staggered terms, two-term limit, quarterly meetings, and subject-to-appropriations expense reimbursement. Retained all five drafted titles.

headings.title: Exemption for independent individual home health providers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text, 1983/1990 history note, and January 1, 1991 effective date. Exempts individuals personally providing home health services who are not under the direct control of, working for, and employed by a home health agency.

headings.title: Exemption for prayer or spiritual-healing religious agencies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and effective-date note. Exempts persons or organizations conducting a home health agency by and for adherents of a recognized church, denomination, or sect providing care relying on prayer or spiritual healing.

headings.title: Exemptions for section 208.152(1)(19) and section 192.2000(2)(18) providers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text, effective-date note, and footnote noting section 3.060 renumbering of section 208.152(1)(18) to (19) in 2018 H.B. 1516. Exempts providers furnishing services under section 208.152(1)(19) or in-home services under section 192.2000(2)(18).

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections, 1983/1990 (effective 1-1-91) history notes, and the footnote explaining section 3.060 renumbering of section 208.152(1)(18) to (19) in 2018 H.B. 1516; verified all checksums and fingerprints. Confirmed exact cross-references in subsection 3 without inferring external categories. Retained all three drafted titles.

headings.title: Website posting of home health surveys, disputes, and correction plans
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(4) plus 2003 history note. Requires DHSS website posting of recent home health surveys, deficiency findings and effects (withholding disputed surveys until resolved and posting requested agency responses), proposed correction plans, federal three-year survey links, and copy-request instructions.

headings.title: Exception for HIPAA-prohibited website disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 2003 history note. Clarifies that section 197.478 does not require posting any information prohibited from disclosure under federal HIPAA.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections including subdivisions 1(1)-(4) and 2003 history note; verified exact checksums and both subsection fingerprints. Revised subsection 2 title to clarify that section 197.478 does not require posting HIPAA-prohibited information on DHSS's website; retained subsection 1 title covering recent surveys, withheld disputed surveys, correction plans, federal summary link, and copy instructions.

headings.title: Employee disqualification list placement and section-specific definitions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 2003 history note. Requires DHSS to place chapter 197 entity employees finally determined under section 192.2490 to have knowingly or recklessly abused or neglected a patient on an employee disqualification list, incorporating section 198.006 definitions of abuse/neglect and defining 'knowingly' and 'recklessly' for this section only.

headings.title: Compilation and maintenance matching section 192.2490 procedures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 2003 history note. Directs DHSS to compile and maintain the chapter 197 employee disqualification list in the same manner as the section 192.2490 list.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and 2003 history note; verified exact checksums and both subsection fingerprints. Checked chapter 197 licensed-entity scope, final section 192.2490 determination requirement, section 198.006 abuse/neglect cross-reference, section-only definitions of "knowingly" and "recklessly", and parallel list compilation/maintenance. Retained both drafted titles.
